evidence.note: Add one distinct physical tee platform visible in the forest opening northwest of the inherited placeholders. Retain the two old unverified pads because tree canopy prevents establishing absence. The visible platform is about 355m from the green, so a forward/middle tee is plausible; championship tee identity and route start must not be inferred from this platform.
Three actual oval tee platforms, ordered back to forward; inner cut surfaces replace the rectangular approximations.
Three visible tee surfaces: the separate western back platform and two inner surfaces on the elongated built terrace alongside the path. The legacy model retained only one misplaced pad.
Narrow rear platform partly shaded on its northeastern lip; round forward platform is clear. Former rectangles were substantially displaced into the tree line.
Three visible platforms. The inherited fourth small rectangle sat in the fairway with no discrete tee surface; fairway tee marker positions remain a separate measurement.
Four physical platforms are visible along the diagonal terrace, including the small forward oval. Inner close-mown areas exclude the broad dry collars.
Long rear platform north of the shelter and separate forward oval southwest of it. The second inherited rectangle lay on ordinary turf between these actual platforms.
Three physical platforms follow the west side of the path. Their geometry is narrower and more elongated than the original rectangles.

Rear tee is the close-mown platform in the forest beside the path, and the small forward tee sits by the pond north of the bridge. The inherited adjacent pair near the back tee missed this forward platform.

Actual close-mown landing fairway and approach follow the northwest forest corridor. The old long polygon entered the trees, and its second disconnected polygon covered forest beside the assumed tees; neither describes visible fairway.
Inner mowing boundary of the curved landing fairway and green entrance, excluding dry rough near the tees and broad striped collars.

Fairway dogleg follows the mown corridor around the central rocky wooded island; the broad semi-rough transfer area beside the tees is excluded. Mown lower lobe and upper landing segment remain one connected fairway.
Par-3 approach is the small close-mown tongue south of the putting surface; the old long quadrilateral described rough between tees and green.

Drought-stressed fairway follows the persistent mowing boundary; brown turf is retained where the mowing edge remains visible. The route bends south around the prominent exposed rock near the green. Surface contrast is weaker than on irrigated greens.

Visible inner fairway mowing contour across the dry central slope. Dry/bare turf remains part of the fairway where mowing boundaries establish it; rough and isolated rock south of the mowing line are excluded.

Long mown fairway runs from its rounded southeastern landing end to the green entrance, independently of the separate tee platforms. The old polygon included rough, woodland and a false eastward extension to the tees.
Par-3 approach is the short-cut tongue southwest of the green. The long former fairway polygon was the semi-rough corridor between the physical tees and green.
Two clearly separated fairway mowing surfaces on opposite sides of the bridge/pond gap. Broad outer rough and the tee-to-fairway lead-in are excluded; no polygon crosses the water gap.

unresolved.reason: Only the added mown platform northwest of the old placeholders can be resolved. Retain the two inherited canopy-obscured pads and existing back route start as unverified. Championship/back tee location and any additional platforms require club/survey confirmation.
Physical tee turf is mapped; five-colour assignments and permanent measured tee points cannot be established reliably from these orthophotos.
